Measured: order [maxAlpha, maxIdx, minAlpha, minIdx] put the immediates in the target's exact sequence -- `li 0` @0x14, `li 0` @0x18, `li 255` @0x1c, `li 0` @0x20, closing both IMMEDIATE rows -- while assigning the four to a scattered set instead of the descending run r31/r30/r29/r28. `savedregs.py game/sfx/psfx PlayerDoWeapTrail` read on that P2 object gives each web's defining instruction: maximumAlpha `@0x14 li r25,0`, maximumIndex `@0x18 li r31,0`, minimumAlpha `@0x1c li r24,255`, minimumIndex `@0x20 li r30,0`, with the parameter copy promoted to `@0x10 mr r28,r3` and lastIndex to `@0x28 lwz r29,2048(r3)` -- against the target's `@0x14 li r31,0`, `@0x18 li r30,0`, `@0x1c li r29,255`, `@0x20 li r28,0`, `@0x10 mr r26,r3`, `@0x28 lwz r27,2048(r3)`. The next lane should attack the NUMBERING with a lever that does not touch the four (their declaration order is fixed by the emission requirement above): move `lastIndex`, `slot`, `offset`, `index` or the parameter's own web in the declaration list under the target-derived order and watch `savedregs.py --uses`, rather than permuting the four again.
